transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, I'm sorry to take up your time, I know there are people with much worse problems. I just... I came in because I'm tired all the time. And I know I'm a teacher, so being tired is kind of part of the job, right? But it's not the normal teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day tired. It's more like... even after a full night's sleep, I really have to push myself through grading, and making dinner, and just getting ready for the next morning. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely miserable or crying all the time. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. Most days, I can still put on a smile for my students and get through the lessons just fine. I always make sure I'm doing my best for them. 

But... I guess, underneath that, there is this sort of... gray, flat feeling? It just kind of follows me home at the end of the day. And it makes things I usually love, like working in my garden or doing my watercolors, just seem really... far away. Like I can't quite connect with them right now. I hope that makes sense? I'm not sure if that's exactly what you mean by sad, but I hope I'm answering your question right.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, it's been a little while now. I'd say... maybe around two years? Two years and a couple of months, give or take. 

It kind of started around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine just sort of shifted, you know? And I think I just haven't quite adjusted as well as I should have. I mean, it's really nice having him home more, and I definitely don't want to sound ungrateful for that. It's just... a big change. 

I'm sorry, I know two years sounds like a really long time to just let something go before asking for help. I probably should have come in sooner, right? I just kept thinking I would bounce back on my own and didn't want to be a bother.
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

Um... well, I guess it's kind of like what I was saying a minute ago about my gardening and watercolors? I definitely haven't completely stopped doing them, I promise. I know it's really important to keep up with hobbies, so I do still try to make time for them on the weekends. I really don't want you to think I just sit around the house doing nothing all day. 

It's just... maybe I don't get that same spark from them right now? Like, I'll get my paints out, but then I just sort of stare at the paper and end up putting them away again after a few minutes. Does that... does that count as losing interest? I'm not entirely sure, I hope I'm answering that right.
Have you experienced any changes in your appetite or weight?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I've always tried to be pretty good about making sure I eat regular meals, especially since I need the energy for the kids at school. I wouldn't want to skip lunch and get grumpy with them! 

So, I think my eating habits are mostly the same, and my clothes still fit the way they usually do. I haven't noticed any big changes or anything. Is... is that what you were looking for? I hope it's okay that I don't have anything to report for that one.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about things lately?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, obviously, there's always a little bit of everyday stress with teaching—just, you know, wanting to make sure I'm doing a good job for my students and keeping up with the grading. But I really wouldn't call it anxiety or anything like that. 

I try really hard not to let myself get too worked up over things. I'd hate to be one of those people who is constantly worrying and stressing everyone else out around them, you know? So... I think I'm doing okay in that department. I hope it's a good thing that I don't have that to add to the list? I just really haven't noticed feeling particularly anxious.
Would you say your feelings of being tired and disconnected from activities are mild, moderate, or severe?

Um... I would definitely say mild. Yes, just mild. I really don't want to exaggerate or make it sound worse than it actually is, you know? I mean, I'm still getting up and going to work every day, and I'm still taking care of my students. I'm definitely not falling apart or anything! 

It's really just... a little bit of a slump, I guess. Nothing I can't push through when I need to. So, I think "mild" is the best word for it. Does that... does that sound right to you, based on what I've been saying? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family members since you started feeling this way?

Um... well, I wouldn't say there have been any huge changes, really. I mean, I'm still showing up for my family, of course, and making sure I'm there for them. I would never want to let them down. 

I guess... maybe I've pulled back just a tiny bit from some of the extra things? Like, I used to do more mentoring with the newer teachers, and I haven't been going out to lunch or social things with my friends quite as often. And I haven't really been doing the little creative hobbies I used to do on the weekends, the things that used to make my life feel a bit more full. 

But it's not like I'm ignoring anyone or being a bad friend! I just... I've been a little more quiet lately, I suppose. I hope that doesn't sound too awful? I really am trying to be there for the people who matter most.
Has this feeling of being tired and disconnected from activities been constant over the past two years, or have you had periods where you felt better?

Um... well, I guess it's been pretty constant, really. I mean, I always try to put on a brave face and keep things upbeat, but... yeah, if I'm being completely honest, it's been going on for about two years and two months now. 

It sort of started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine just changed, and... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about him being home or about our life, because I'm absolutely not! It's just that ever since that transition, this little slump has kind of just stayed with me. I haven't really had a stretch where it completely went away. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you still enjoy things that you used to find pleasurable, or has the pleasure gone away?

Um... well, I wouldn't say the pleasure is completely gone! I really do try to stay positive. Most days, I can still smile for my students and, you know, get through the lessons just fine. I always make sure they get the best of me, and I don't think anyone at school would even notice anything is off.

But... I suppose, if I'm being totally honest... underneath that, it feels like there’s this sort of... gray, flat feeling? And it kind of just follows me home at the end of the day. When I finally have time for my garden or my watercolors—things I usually just love doing—they just seem a bit... far away right now. Like I can't quite reach that happy feeling they usually give me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely ungrateful for the good things in my life? I really am trying my best to enjoy them. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a helpful answer.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight over the past two years?

Oh, um, no, I haven't. My weight has stayed pretty much exactly the same, I think. I always try to make sure I'm eating properly and making decent meals, you know, to keep my energy up for the kids at school. So, no, no major weight loss or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good sign? I mean, I really do try to take good care of my physical health, so I haven't noticed any big changes on the scale. Is that... does that help rule anything bad out? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you had to make any significant changes to your daily routine or responsibilities due to the way you've been feeling?

Um... well, no, not the really big responsibilities. I mean, I’m still showing up for my students every single day, and of course, I'm always there for my family. I make sure all the important things get done, I promise! 

But... I suppose if I really think about it, I have sort of quietly pulled back from some of the extras. Just to, you know, conserve my energy a little bit? Like, I used to do some mentoring at school, and I've stepped away from that for now. And... I guess I haven't been going to as many social outings with friends, or keeping up with those creative routines that usually keep my life feeling so full. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm dropping the ball! I'm still working really hard at my job and at home. It's just... my day-to-day is a little smaller than it used to be, I guess. Is that... is that the kind of change you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in and look forward to?

Um... well, yes, I think so! I really try to focus on the good things, you know? Like, seeing my students understand a new concept—that always brings a little smile to my face. And I still really enjoy making dinner for my family. It's nice to just be together at the end of the day. 

I mean, I know I said earlier that my gardening and painting feel a little... distant right now, but I still like the *idea* of them! I still look forward to the weekends, even if I end up just resting more than I planned. I really am trying to keep a positive outlook and find joy in the little things. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope it shows that I'm not completely giving up on things or anything like that. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now feel like you're just going through the motions?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to put my whole heart into everything I do, especially with my students and my family. I would hate to ever just... phone it in, you know? 

Even if I'm a little tired sometimes, I really make an effort to be fully present. I don't feel like I'm just sleepwalking through my day or faking it. I really do still care about the things I'm doing, even the small things. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I just want to assure you that I'm still trying my very best to stay engaged and not let anyone down. Is that... is it okay that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression.
Would you describe your feelings of sadness or disconnection as being present most of the day or nearly every day?

Um... well, I wouldn't want you to think I'm just walking around sad all the time or anything like that! I mean, most days I can absolutely still smile for my students, and I get through all my lessons just fine. I always make sure they get the best of me. 

But... I guess if I'm really looking at it, underneath all that, it does feel like there’s this sort of... this quiet, gray, flat feeling? And it just kind of follows me home when the school day is done. It's just there in the background, making things I usually love, like my garden or my watercolors, seem a little... far away right now. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm complaining too much! I really am trying my best to stay positive and push through it. Does that... does that make sense for what you were asking? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right.
How many days a week would you say you experience this gray, flat feeling?

Um... well, it's hard to put an exact number on it, to be honest. I really try not to dwell on it too much, you know? I want to focus on the days where I'm feeling good and productive. 

I guess... maybe a few days a week? But really, it's not like it stops me from doing what I need to do. I still get up, I still go to work, I still take care of my family. It's just... maybe a little more noticeable on some days than others, especially when I'm tired. 

But I promise it's not every single day or anything! I definitely have good days where I don't feel it as much. I hope that's okay? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. Am I giving you the kind of answer you need?
Have your symptoms lasted for more than two years?

Um... wow, two years? I mean, I guess when you put it like that... I suppose it has been a while. I wouldn't want you to think I've just been sitting around feeling sorry for myself all this time! I really have been trying to manage it on my own.

But, um... if I really think back, I guess it started around... maybe two years and two months ago? Right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine just kind of shifted, and I think I just got a little overwhelmed trying to keep everything running smoothly for everyone. 

I really didn't want to make a fuss about it, you know? I figured it was just an adjustment period and I just needed to try harder to be positive. I hope it's not bad that I waited this long to say something? I just really wanted to handle it myself and not be a burden. Is it... is it normal for it to linger like that when there's a big change at home?
Would you say that your gray, flat feeling is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Um... oh, definitely mild. I really want to be clear about that, it's—it's very mild. I wouldn't call it severe at all! I don't want you to think I'm incapacitated or, you know, unable to function. Like I said, I'm still teaching my classes and making sure my students get what they need from me. 

It's just... it's just a very light, mild sort of grayness. Just enough to be there, but not enough to ruin a day, if that makes sense? I really try to just push past it and keep a smile on. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just don't want to sound like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. Does mild sound like the right word to you, based on what I've been saying?
Can you clarify if there have been any periods, even brief ones, where you felt completely back to normal since this gray, flat feeling started?

Um... completely back to normal? Well, I mean, I definitely have good moments! I really do. Like when my students finally grasp a difficult concept, or when my husband and I have a nice dinner... I feel happy then. I really try to focus on those moments.

But as for feeling completely, 100% like my old self, for like... a whole stretch of time? I'm... I'm honestly not entirely sure. I don't really keep track of it that closely, because I don't want to dwell on the negative, you know? I just try to keep moving forward. 

I guess I haven't really noticed a long period where the grayness is completely, totally gone. It's usually just sort of... hovering in the background, even on the better days. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want it to sound like I'm complaining or that I don't appreciate the good things in my life. I do, I promise! Am I explaining that okay?
Has your gray, flat feeling persisted for the majority of the day, for most days, over the past two weeks?

Um... well, yes, I suppose if I look at the last two weeks... it has been there most days. For a good part of the day, I guess. But I really want to make sure you know that I'm still doing my job! Most days, I can still put on a smile for my students and get through all the lessons without them ever noticing a thing. I really pride myself on being there for them. 

It's just... underneath that, it feels like there’s this gray, flat feeling that just sort of... follows me home. And then things I normally love, like my garden or my watercolors, they just seem so... far away? Like I just can't quite connect with them right now. 

I really try not to let it take over, though. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just giving up the second I walk through my front door? I really am trying my best to stay upbeat and keep things normal. Is it... is it okay that I can push through at work but still feel that way underneath?
